stories.title: Pakistan liquor sales continue despite strict laws and minority concerns
stories.summary:
The ongoing sale of alcoholic beverages across Pakistan, including approximately 150 shops in Sindh and nearly 70 in Karachi, has sparked intense debate regarding legal enforcement and regulatory loopholes. Although the nation's legal framework strictly prohibits Muslim citizens from consuming alcohol and restricts purchases to authorized non-Muslims under the Hudood Ordinance, reports indicate that a significant portion of licensed alcohol reaches unauthorized individuals.

The commercial scale of the industry has drawn heightened scrutiny, highlighted by a 55 percent increase in revenue collected through Sindh alcohol duties in 2022 compared to the preceding year. Wholesalers, retail wine shops, and import distribution agents operate throughout the province, backed by a 2017 Sindh High Court ban that was subsequently overturned by a three-member Supreme Court bench, allowing licensed sales to persist.

Representatives from religious minority communities have strongly criticized the current licensing framework. Atam Prakash of the FPCCI Minorities Committee and Saleem Michael of the Christian Helpline argue that their religious beliefs forbid alcohol consumption and that minority identities are being unfairly exploited to facilitate sales. They have also alleged that influential figures and politicians acquire permits using the names of non-Muslim employees.

This ongoing situation highlights deep concerns about regulatory oversight, the verification of eligible buyers, and the monitoring of distribution networks. The persistent availability of alcohol throughout the year continues to raise critical questions about how current laws are enforced and who is driving the actual demand.

stories.title: US midterm elections arrive with control of Congress at stake
stories.summary:
United States congressional candidates and President Donald Trump made their final appeals to voters ahead of Tuesday's high-stakes midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress for the remainder of Trump's term. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are contested. While Democrats are favored to retake the House, Senate control remains fiercely contested, carrying immense implications for future federal court appointments and potential investigations into the administration.

Tensions flared across multiple states on the eve of the vote. In California, the Supreme Court swiftly rejected an attempt by the Trump Justice Department to block the counting of mail-in ballots from over 20,000 registered voters alleged to be non-citizens. A federal judge also ordered the administration to stop demanding that California segregate these specific ballots. Meanwhile, in Michigan, Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed aimed to become the first Muslim elected to the Senate, facing Republican Mike Rogers in a race marked by intense political friction and a record $2.4 million single-day fundraising haul for El-Sayed.

In Alaska, a federal lawsuit seeking to block election certification over a voter confusion issue involving two candidates named Sullivan was dismissed by a judge. The Justice Department had intervened following reports that a Democratic campaign recruited a spoiler candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. to challenge Republican incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan. Senator Sullivan stated he would accept the election results despite an ongoing FBI inquiry into a campaign donation.

President Trump spent his final days campaigning vigorously across 20 states over 32 days, concluding with a speech in Washington focusing on public works and infrastructure projects. As voters head to the polls, the outcome of the midterms will critically impact the political balance of power in Washington and shape the legislative landscape for the final two years of Trump's presidency.

stories.title: German pediatrician goes on trial for sexually abusing seventy children
stories.summary:
A 46-year-old pediatrician in eastern Germany went on trial facing more than 130 criminal charges related to the sexual abuse of over 70 children. The alleged offenses took place over a period exceeding a decade, specifically between 2013 and 2025, while the physician was employed at medical clinics located in the eastern German towns of Nauen and Rathenow.

During the court proceedings, after the charges were formally read, the defendant spoke briefly to address the allegations. He acknowledged the majority of the acts, reaffirmed earlier confessions he had made regarding the crimes, and expressed a profound sense of guilt for his actions.

According to the documentation of the case, the doctor primarily targeted male patients. In most instances, he entered the rooms of his young victims and instructed them to undress under the guise of medical necessity, subsequently taking photographs and occasionally videos of them.

The commencement of the trial brings public attention to the extensive scale of the abuse committed within clinical settings over many years. The proceedings will continue to address the full scope of the charges brought against the physician in connection with the victims.

stories.title: UN reports warn exceeding 1.5C global warming brings irreversible ice damage
stories.summary:
Two United Nations reports released on Monday warned that exceeding 1.5 degrees Celsius of global warming will trigger large-scale and irreversible consequences for the Earth's frozen regions, including glaciers, sea ice, and permafrost. The landmark 2015 Paris Agreement aims to hold warming well below 2 degrees Celsius while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees Celsius to avert the worst impacts of climate change. Currently, global warming has already reached 1.37 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, with the European Copernicus network warning that the 1.5-degree threshold could be breached around 2030.

The report titled “Overshoot and the Cryosphere,” authored by 80 scientists and led by glaciologist James Kirkham, emphasizes that current warming levels are already unsafe for the Arctic, Antarctic, mountain glaciers, and polar oceans. Scientists explain that returning temperatures to safe levels after an overshoot will be exceptionally slow, taking decades to centuries for oceans and ice to recover. Even if global temperatures eventually fall back below 1.5 degrees Celsius, preventing a temporary overshoot is vital because every extra fraction of a degree causes more devastating impacts, such as accelerated sea level rise, severe flooding, and widespread water shortages.

A second report, “State of the Cryosphere 2026. The Cost of Overshoot,” highlights that failing to curb emissions could lead to warming of 2.8 degrees Celsius into the next century. Under such a scenario, sea levels could surge by up to five centimeters a year by 2150, compared to the current 0.45 centimeters, while thawing permafrost could release annual carbon dioxide emissions equivalent to the output of the United States. Experts stress that temporarily exceeding the Paris Agreement targets makes global climate goals even more urgent, requiring an accelerated transition away from fossil fuels to achieve net-zero emissions by mid-century.

stories.title: Fertiliser Curbs Disrupt Rabi Sowing Across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary:
Chashma Sugar Mills has formally complained to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi regarding severe fertilizer shortages caused by restricted supply chains. In an official letter, Senior Director Iskander Khan stated that the company received field reports indicating the fertilizer industry halted dispatches to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan following an SRO issued by the Ministry of Interior.

The timing of these supply restrictions has created critical challenges because the autumn and Rabi sowing season is currently underway. Khan emphasized that fertilizer is a vital input required to ensure healthy crop growth and high productivity for major agricultural yields in the province.

Any delays or disruptions in securing this essential agricultural input threaten to diminish crop yields significantly. This situation also places an added financial burden on local farmers and risks exacerbating food insecurity throughout the entire province.

Furthermore, Khan warned that the reduced crop productivity would negatively impact the supply of sugarcane to regional sugar mills. Authorities enacted these strict supply limitations because certain categories of fertilizer can be utilized in manufacturing explosives, raising security concerns that hostile actors might obtain the materials from commercial vendors.

stories.title: Afghan Taliban Express Concern Over US Deportation Plans Through Pakistan
stories.summary:
Afghanistan's Taliban authorities have raised serious concerns regarding reported Washington plans to deport over 150 Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan via Pakistan. According to US media reports and local advocacy groups, the group includes relatives of individuals who assisted United States forces prior to their withdrawal from the country in 2021.

Foreign ministry spokesman Abdul Qahar Balkhi released a statement noting the serious concern of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan over the intended deportations of refugees who have not yet secured legal residency documents within Pakistan. Human rights advocates have warned that relocating these former allies and their families back to the region could place their lives in immediate danger.

Following their return to power, Taliban authorities announced a general amnesty for all Afghans who previously worked alongside Western-backed forces and governments. Officials have reiterated assurances throughout the year that former adversaries can safely return to their homeland.

Despite these official guarantees, the United Nations has documented multiple reports detailing extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detentions, and other abuses against returning individuals. The immigration measures follow broader crackdowns by the administration of President Donald Trump, which previously issued travel bans for several nations including Afghanistan and sought to terminate deportation protections for Afghans holding special immigrant visas.

stories.title: Imported Wheat Fails to Lower Retail Flour Prices in Pakistan
stories.summary:
The arrival of imported wheat shipments has driven down open market grain prices, yet consumers across Pakistan continue to face high costs for flour and bread products. On October 28, the first vessel carrying 51,000 tonnes of wheat docked at the port, causing open market wheat rates to drop from Rs140 to Rs130 per kilogram. A second vessel carrying 58,132 tonnes was scheduled to arrive soon after, causing market prices to fluctuate between Rs132 and Rs137 per kilogram depending on the source.

Millers had previously increased flour prices by Rs20 per kilogram before lowering them slightly ahead of the grain imports. Current mill prices for flour No. 2.5, Maida, and fine flour stand at Rs156, Rs168, and Rs171 per kilogram respectively, down from earlier October highs. However, retail consumers have experienced no financial relief, as prices for baked goods like Chapati, Naan, Sheermal, and Qulcha remain entirely unchanged. Tandoor owners note that extremely high liquefied petroleum gas prices ranging from Rs500 to Rs550 per kilogram have completely offset the benefits of cheaper flour.

Wholesalers report that government regulators have failed to enforce lower retail prices despite the dip in open market rates. Experts warn that importing 750,000 tonnes of wheat will fall well short of the nation's two million tonne demand gap, especially since new harvests from Sindh and Punjab will not arrive until between March and May. Low-income workers earning under Rs50,000 are spending nearly all their earnings on basic food items, leaving little for education and other family needs.

Consumers in Karachi and Hyderabad currently pay the highest flour prices nationwide, with a 20kg bag reaching up to Rs3,540 in Karachi according to the Sensitive Price Index ending October 29. Hyderabad follows closely with bags priced between Rs3,360 and Rs3,400. Cities like Islamabad, Rawalpindi, and Lahore show lower average rates, while Sargodha records the cheapest 10kg bag at Rs1,223. Analysts point out that Karachi's complete reliance on external grain shipments from Sindh contributes heavily to its persistently inflated local prices.

stories.title: شمالی کوریا نے بائنانس پر 6.3 ارب ڈالر کی ہیکنگ میں ملوث ہونے کی تردید کر دی
stories.summary:
شمالی کوریا نے کرپٹو کرنسی ایکسچینج بائنانس پر 6.3 ارب ڈالر مالیت کے ریکارڈ سائبر حملے میں ملوث ہونے کے الزامات کو مسترد کرتے ہوئے انہیں بے بنیاد قرار دیا ہے۔ شمالی کوریا کے رہنما کم جونگ اُن کی بہن کم یو جونگ نے کہا ہے کہ یہ الزامات ملک کی ساکھ کو نقصان پہنچانے کی امریکی کوشش ہیں۔

امریکہ کے ایف بی آئی، سیکرٹ سروس اور سائبر سکیورٹی تجزیہ کاروں کا دعویٰ ہے کہ یہ حملہ ریاستی سرپرستی میں کام کرنے والے شمالی کوریا کے ہیکنگ گروپ ٹریڈر ٹریٹر نے کیا۔ بائنانس کے مطابق یہ ہیکنگ ممکنہ طور پر تاریخ کا سب سے بڑا کرپٹو حملہ ہے، جس کا آغاز ایک انجینیئر کے متاثرہ لیپ ٹاپ سے ہوا۔

بائنانس نے اعلان کیا ہے کہ وہ اس حملے سے ہونے والے سو فیصد نقصانات کا ازالہ خود کرے گا اور اب تک چرائے گئے اثاثوں کا نوے فیصد حصہ بحال کر دیا گیا ہے۔ کمپنی کا کہنا ہے کہ اس مالی نقصان کا بوجھ صارفین پر نہیں ڈالا جائے گا بلکہ کارپوریٹ فنڈز سے پورا کیا جائے گا۔

چین انالیسس اور ٹی آر ایم لیبز سمیت کئی تجزیاتی اداروں نے بھی اس واقعے کا تعلق شمالی کوریا سے جوڑا ہے۔ ادھر مغربی سکیورٹی اداروں کا ماننا ہے کہ اس طرح کے سائبر حملوں سے حاصل ہونے والی رقوم شمالی کوریا کے جوہری ہتھیاروں اور میزائل پروگراموں کی مالی معاونت میں استعمال ہوتی ہیں۔

stories.title: US and Iran Signal Diplomatic Progress Amid Continuing Regional Tensions
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump indicated progress in ongoing negotiations with Iran aimed at preventing a full return to conflict, while Tehran reported intensive diplomatic exchanges and offered conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. These diplomatic developments unfolded just ahead of US midterm elections where Republicans sought to maintain congressional control amid voter frustration over the conflict and rising fuel prices. Trump stated on social media that a settlement could happen soon because Tehran desires an agreement.

Despite the optimistic diplomatic signals, the Wall Street Journal reported that the United States had recently executed a series of limited, secret strikes against Iran, coinciding with reports of five rapid explosions on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi confirmed that indirect talks were moving forward through mediators like Qatar and Pakistan, while Vice President JD Vance expressed optimism about securing an agreement. Meanwhile, Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Beijing to advocate for political solutions, ceasefires, and peaceful resolutions through diplomacy.

Iran stated it is prepared to reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to specific demands outlined in September. These conditions include halting the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian financial assets, lifting oil sanctions, and ending counter-blockades against Iranian ports. Tehran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei emphasized that implementing the plan quickly would demonstrate Iran's good-faith approach to regional stability.

Araghchi asserted that Washington must accept a newly agreed transit route between Iran and Oman, reduce American troop presence in the region, and remove recently imposed economic sanctions. Concurrently, Trump and other US officials maintained strong rhetoric regarding nuclear sites like Pickaxe mountain, while Iranian authorities warned that any foreign aggression would trigger a powerful, immediate, and comprehensive response.

stories.title: United States Conducts Secret Strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island
stories.summary:
The United States carried out a military strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island, according to a report published by the Wall Street Journal. The operation on the largest island in the Strait of Hormuz represents the latest in a series of covert, limited assaults conducted by Washington against Iran over the preceding weeks. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported that five explosions happened in rapid succession on the island, with residents observing two aircraft in the airspace. The Pentagon directed inquiries to the US Central Command, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Unnamed officials characterized the small-scale assaults as defensive actions aimed at stopping Iran from blocking commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. This vital conduit for oil shipments has remained largely obstructed since the war began in late February. Washington kept the attacks out of the public eye to avoid signaling any intent to restart major combat operations. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump remarked that an agreement with Tehran could materialize, coinciding with US midterm elections. The Strait of Hormuz blockade had previously driven up energy costs, but oil prices fell by over seven percent following optimism about a potential end to the conflict.

Earlier on Monday, US Vice President JD Vance expressed cautious optimism that a deal could prevent Trump from ordering fresh strikes after the midterm elections. Vance communicated with Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, through a letter sent the previous week. Although the White House provided minimal details about the correspondence, Trump noted that the letter centered on delivering medical supplies and related assistance to Iran.

stories.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio Discusses Venezuelan Electoral Reforms
stories.summary:
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Venezuelan Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco at the State Department on Monday to discuss institutional reforms aimed at establishing future free, fair, and credible elections. The discussions centered on progress in Venezuelan-led reconciliation talks under United States oversight. This diplomatic engagement follows a deadly US military raid ordered by President Donald Trump in early January, which resulted in the seizure and transfer of ousted leader Nicolas Maduro and his wife to New York to face trial.

Following Maduro's removal, his former vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, assumed power as interim president. The Trump administration has expressed support for ongoing negotiations between Rodriguez's government and various opposition groups regarding an overhaul of Venezuela's electoral council and top court. However, these talks exclude Maria Corina Machado and her Vente Venezuela movement. Venezuelan opposition figures have noted that Washington suggested holding presidential elections next year.

In addition to electoral matters, Minister Blanco met with US Treasury chief Scott Bessent on Monday to discuss boosting energy production and securing new investments in Venezuela. Interim President Rodriguez's administration has already signed various agreements with oil and gas companies with US backing. Rubio stated last week that Venezuela's current electoral infrastructure was designed to rig elections and requires rapid replacement.

While the Trump administration engages with the interim government, these actions have drawn international criticism. In January, the United Nations human rights office stated that US intervention in Venezuela violated international law. Additionally, human rights advocates have characterized the focus on exploiting Venezuelan oil as an imperialist approach.

stories.title: China Market Regulator Pledges Support for Hong Kong Listings
stories.summary:
China's market regulator announced plans to strengthen cross-border regulation and establish an institutional environment that supports domestic companies listing in Hong Kong. The announcement was made by Li Chao, vice chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, during an appearance in Hong Kong.

The regulatory official made the remarks on Tuesday while speaking at the Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit. Alongside supporting corporate listings in the territory, Li emphasized that the regulatory body will target fraud and illicit cross-border capital activities.

The stated initiatives from the Chinese securities regulator are intended to deepen financial integration and regulatory oversight between mainland China and Hong Kong. Following reports of this regulatory support, China stocks experienced an upward movement, though bond market sentiment was impacted by concerns related to Huafa.

The summit provided a platform for financial leaders to discuss cross-border economic strategies and regulatory frameworks. The announcement highlights ongoing efforts by Chinese authorities to balance the encouragement of international capital-raising avenues with stricter enforcement against financial misconduct.

stories.title: Pakistan Faces Severe Fuel and Gas Storage Deficit Challenges
stories.summary:
Pakistan faced severe energy vulnerabilities following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz on February 28, 2026. QatarEnergy declared force majeure, cutting off supplies for Pakistan, which sourced almost all of its liquefied natural gas from Qatar. Because the country lacked adequate gas and oil storage capabilities, authorities had to release withheld gas and ask Saudi Arabia to reroute crude through the Red Sea. Years of structural shifts, including IMF-driven tariff changes, had previously caused industrial consumers to switch to solar power, leading to domestic gas curtailments of up to 350 mmcfd just before the crisis.

Policymakers have long recognized the need for storage, yet little action has been taken. Gas storage relies on pumping surplus fuel into depleted reservoirs, a solution studied by the Asian Development Bank as early as 2004 in Badin and again in 2022. Feasibility tenders were issued in 2024 and in early 2026, but even if built, the initial facility will only cover 12 days of consumption instead of the recommended month. Oil storage has suffered similar failures because marketing companies are not paid to hold reserves and face potential losses during fortnightly price revisions, while the state has never built a strategic reserve.

Efforts to attract foreign suppliers to maintain bonded fuel storage without paying duty have also stalled since being approved in 2023. Foreign traders are reluctant to register local offices in Pakistan, fear the government might block exports during shortages, and must navigate conflicting rules from five different bodies including customs, the regulator, the central bank, and ministries. Although the government has reopened the policy, it has failed to attract investment.

The lack of storage forces the country to repeatedly pay premium prices for emergency cargoes during disruptions. Experts emphasize that the government must establish clear rules, quick licensing, and single-office dispute resolution rather than spending public funds, ensuring the country is prepared for future supply shocks.

stories.title: Anti-Terrorism Court Grants Pre-Arrest Bail to Four PTI Leaders
stories.summary:
An Anti-Terrorism Court in Islamabad granted pre-arrest bail on Monday to four Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf leaders in connection with cases stemming from a November 26 protest and a demonstration outside the Supreme Court. ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain approved the bail applications after a hearing, directing each politician to furnish surety bonds of Rs5,000.

The politicians granted relief include former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, Atif Khan, Latif Khosa, and Faisal Amin Gandapur. According to the court order, Mr. Qaiser received bail in nine cases, Mr. Gandapur in six, Mr. Khan in four, and Mr. Khosa in three. The court had previously dismissed their earlier pre-arrest bail requests because the leaders repeatedly failed to appear for hearings.

Following the prior dismissal, the four PTI leaders filed fresh pre-arrest bail applications, which the court ultimately accepted after hearing arguments from their legal counsel. The cases against them involve security and protest-related charges originating from late last year.

In related legal developments, the Islamabad High Court has scheduled a hearing for November 5 regarding a petition filed by members of the National Dialogue Committee. The petition seeks official permission for leaders to meet incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, at Adiala jail.

stories.title: Cyclone Murasu Strikes India's Eastern Coast, Prompting Mass Evacuations
stories.summary:
India's eastern coast faced its second severe tropical storm in a week when Cyclone Murasu made landfall on Tuesday, according to the nation's weather department. The severe cyclonic system crossed the coastline of Andhra Pradesh between 03:30 and 05:30 local time, bringing sustained winds of 100 to 110 kilometers per hour alongside gusts reaching up to 120 kilometers per hour. 

Authorities initiated evacuation measures on Monday, targeting approximately 30,000 residents in Andhra Pradesh to ensure public safety as the storm approached from the Bay of Bengal. Prakhar Jain, Managing Director of the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority, confirmed that no injuries or fatalities have been recorded thus far, though the weather event uprooted several electric poles and trees.

The India Meteorological Department indicated that Andhra Pradesh and the neighboring southern state of Tamil Nadu were expected to bear the brunt of the weather system. The Bay of Bengal frequently generates destructive tropical weather events.

This latest emergency follows closely on the heels of Cyclone Arnab, which the meteorological agency classified as a very severe cyclonic storm and which struck Andhra Pradesh the previous Wednesday, resulting in at least six deaths.

stories.title: Disney Considers Thousands of Layoffs and Deep Budget Cuts, Reports Say
stories.summary:
Walt Disney is reportedly weighing thousands of job reductions and instructing specific managers to achieve annual expenditure reductions of 20 percent, based on information from Bloomberg News citing anonymous sources. This potential restructuring initiative unfolds as executive Josh D’Amaro addresses ongoing hurdles such as falling box office earnings, rising artificial intelligence integration, fierce competition from streaming competitors, and diminished international visitor numbers at the corporation's amusement parks.

Certain operational sectors within the enterprise are anticipated to absorb a greater share of the reductions than others. D’Amaro plans to channel a portion of the resulting savings back into cruise line operations, theme parks, technology infrastructure, and film and television content creation. Disney did not immediately reply to media inquiries submitted outside standard business hours, and the exact count of potentially impacted personnel remains unspecified, though the conglomerate reported an employee total of approximately 231,000 at the conclusion of fiscal 2025.

The organization has previously implemented multiple workforce reductions in recent years to enhance financial performance. These include shedding a small number of personnel across technology and human resources in September, eliminating roughly 1,000 positions in April, cutting several hundred roles throughout 2025, and slashing 7,000 jobs in 2023 under former CEO Bob Iger to achieve $5.5 billion in cost reductions.

Across the broader media and entertainment landscape, companies have similarly turned to downsizing to trim expenditures. Notable examples include Netflix and Skydance, the latter of which finalized its acquisition of larger competitor Warner Bros Discovery earlier in the year.

stories.title: Malaysia Schedules Critical Security Meetings Amid Growing Global Threats
stories.summary:
Malaysia's chief government secretary and central bank governor will convene separate briefings with financial institutions and government departments to enhance national preparedness against potential security risks, the prime minister announced on Tuesday. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim addressed parliament to explain that these proactive steps follow warnings and guidance issued by Canada, Japan, and the European Union urging citizens to maintain food reserves following widespread cyberattacks targeting digital infrastructure and administrative networks throughout Europe and the Western world.

In his parliamentary address, Anwar emphasized that domestic safety, economic stability, and national interests remain vulnerable to external crises. He specifically highlighted ongoing geopolitical friction in the Middle East, events unfolding in Yemen and the Red Sea, and escalating security challenges across Europe as evidence of how international instability can reach Malaysia.

To address these concerns, the nation's National Security Council has already convened. Officials evaluated existing response frameworks, assessed the readiness of security forces, and reviewed inter-agency and ministerial coordination to ensure the country can respond effectively to any unforeseen circumstances.

stories.title: North Korea Tests Strategic Cruise Missile With Dispersal Warhead
stories.summary:
North Korea conducted a military test on Monday involving a strategic cruise missile equipped with a dispersal warhead, according to statements released on Tuesday by the state-run news agency KCNA. 

During the evaluation, military authorities examined the flight performance capabilities of the weapon system, specifically focusing on a vertical strike profile. The test represents the latest in a series of military developments reported by the isolated nation's official media channels.

Pyongyang regularly tests various missile configurations to assess their technical characteristics and operational readiness. State media typically provides brief accounts of these defense milestones following the completion of each exercise.

stories.title: Indian Shares Projected to Rise Amid Easing Oil and Earnings
stories.summary:
Indian equities are anticipated to open higher on Tuesday, extending a three-session winning streak. This positive momentum is supported by robust corporate earnings, declining crude oil prices, and early indications of foreign investors returning to the market, despite ongoing geopolitical concerns.

GIFT Nifty futures stood at 23,523.5 during early morning trading hours, pointing toward a favorable start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index, which closed at 23,440.8 on Monday. Both the Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex surged 1.7% on Monday to achieve their highest closing levels in over five and eight weeks, respectively.

Global crude prices remained flat around $105 per barrel following a significant 7% drop in the prior session. The decrease was driven by talks between Iran and Qatari mediators that sparked optimism for a resolution to the conflict involving the US, Israel, and Iran. Nevertheless, reports of a US strike on Qeshm Island maintained elevated geopolitical tensions.

Foreign portfolio investors were net buyers on Monday with 31.15 billion Indian rupees in inflows, while domestic institutional investors registered a net sell-off of 3.92 billion rupees. Market analysts note that sustained geopolitical de-escalation and lower energy costs could support the ongoing recovery, though negotiation breakdowns or global tech stock weakness could introduce volatility.

Several companies drew specific focus, including Marico, which exceeded quarterly profit forecasts due to reduced copra costs and strong demand. Dr. Reddy's announced that the US FDA granted tentative approval for a generic HIV prevention drug, and Granules India reported a roughly 40% rise in September quarter profit propelled by new product launches and overseas sales.

stories.title: امریکی وسط مدتی انتخابات میں کانگریس کے کنٹرول پر سخت سیاسی جنگ جاری
stories.summary:
امریکہ میں کانگریس کے ایوانِ نمائندگان اور سینیٹ کے اراکین کے انتخاب کے لیے وسط مدتی انتخابات کا انعقاد کیا جا रहा ہے، جن پر صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ کے اقتدار کے بقیہ دو سالوں کی کامیابی یا ناکامی کا دار و مدار ہے۔ اس وقت کانگریس کے دونوں ایوانوں پر صدر ٹرمپ کی جماعت ریپبلکن پارٹی کا کنٹرول قائم ہے، تاہم اپوزیشن جماعت ڈیموکریٹس کو امید ہے کہ وہ موجودہ سیاسی حالات میں کامیابی حاصل کر لیں گے۔

انتخابات سے قبل صدر ٹرمپ کی عوامی مقبولیت میں نمایاں کمی دیکھی گئی ہے، جو اقتدار سنبھالنے کے وقت 50 فیصد سے زائد تھی لیکن اب گر کر تقریباً 38 فیصد تک آ چکی ہے۔ رواں برس فروری میں اسرائیل کے ساتھ مل کر ایران کے خلاف فضائی حملے شروع کرنے اور اس کے نتیجے میں پیٹرول کی قیمتیں چار ڈالر فی گیلن تک پہنچنے سے شہریوں میں معاشی مشکلات بڑھیں، جس نے اس جنگ اور صدر کی پالیسیوں کو غیر مقبول بنا دیا۔

ایوانِ نمائندگان کی تمام 435 نشستوں پر ہر دو سال بعد انتخابات ہوتے ہیں جہاں ریپبلکنز کے پاس انتہائی معمولی اکثریت ہے۔ تاریخی طور پر وسط مدتی انتخابات میں برسراقتدار صدر کی جماعت کو اوسطاً 27 نشستوں کا نقصان اٹھانا پڑتا ہے۔ دوسری جانب، سینیٹ کی 100 رکنی نشستوں میں سے رواں ماہ 35 نشستوں پر مقابلے ہو رہے ہیں جن میں سے سات نشستوں کو غیر یقینی قرار دیا گیا ہے، اور ڈیموکریٹس کو اکثریت کے لیے ان میں سے چار نشستیں جیتنا ہوں گی۔

معاشی مسائل کے علاوہ مہنگائی، اخراجاتِ زندگی، صحت کی سہولیات اور امیگریشن کے معاملات ووٹرز کے لیے سب سے اہم مسائل ہیں۔ اگرچہ رائے عامہ کے جائزوں میں ڈیموکریٹس کی پوزیشن بہتر بتائی جا رہی ہے، لیکن ریپبلکن جماعت کو اکتوبر کے وسط تک تقریباً 32 کروڑ ڈالر اور ٹرمپ کے میگا انک گروپ کے پاس 16 کروڑ ڈالر سے زائد کے فنڈز کی نمایاں مالی برتری حاصل ہے، جسے وہ اشتہاری مہمات پر بھرپور طریقے سے خرچ کر رہے ہیں۔

stories.title: US Dollar Wavers as Oil Slumps and Central Banks Eye Rates
stories.summary:
The US dollar fluctuated alongside plunging oil prices on Tuesday, influenced by emerging diplomatic hopes between the US and Iran alongside easing global inflation concerns. Meanwhile, currency markets braced for a busy week featuring policy decisions from multiple central banks.

Brent crude futures experienced a dramatic single-day slump of over 7% on Monday, triggered by Tehran's confirmation that diplomatic contacts with the US aimed at halting their eight-month conflict were ongoing. The resulting energy price relief dragged longer-dated US Treasury yields lower, though benchmark 10-year Treasury yields remained steady at 4.9145% and 30-year bond yields held at 5.2868% following multi-month lows.

The dollar index dipped to 101.76 after touching a one-month low on Monday. Ongoing artificial intelligence-related stock market slumps and safe-haven demand tied to US midterm election risks offered underlying support to the greenback. The euro gained slightly to trade at $1.1185, while the Japanese yen held flat at 157.915 per dollar during a local holiday.

International central banks prepared to release policy statements, with the Reserve Bank of Australia widely expected to hike its official cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85%, marking its highest level since December 2008. The Australian dollar traded unchanged at $0.7002.

In the United Kingdom, sterling advanced 0.05% to $1.3414 after purchasing managers' index data demonstrated that British manufacturers recorded their strongest output growth in over two years at the start of the final quarter of 2026. Economists surveyed by Reuters anticipate the Bank of England will lift its Bank Rate to 4.0%.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Set for Gains on Oil Drop Amid Technical Resistance
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is projected to open stronger on Tuesday following a sharp decline in international crude oil prices. However, persistent US dollar strength and strong technical barriers are expected to limit the extent of the currency's overall recovery.

Foreign exchange traders indicated that the rupee is likely to open within the 94.75 to 94.78 range against the dollar, following a close of 94.90 on Monday. Brent crude dropped significantly by 11% on Monday, stabilizing near $104.70 in Asian trading, after discussions between Iranian and Qatari officials fostered optimism regarding a potential resolution to the ongoing conflict involving the US, Israel, and Iran.

High energy costs have historically pressured the Indian economy, as the nation imports roughly 90% of its total oil requirements. Elevated prices inflate the import bill, worsen macroeconomic indicators, increase corporate currency hedging demand, and diminish foreign portfolio inflows. The Reserve Bank of India has continually intervened in foreign exchange markets by selling dollars and deploying alternative measures to support the domestic currency.

Market participants noted that while lower oil prices provide vital relief, the 94.50 to 94.70 range poses a formidable zone of technical resistance for the rupee. Additionally, broad weakness across regional Asian currencies—such as the Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso—reflects ongoing investor risk aversion linked to artificial intelligence sector jitters.

Broader Asian equities reflected the cautious sentiment, with MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan falling 0.8% as investors monitored global market reactions and awaited outcomes from US midterm elections.

stories.title: Diplomatic Window Opens for Iran Peace Amid Regional Strain
stories.summary:
As threats of renewed US and Israeli military strikes persist, a parallel diplomatic initiative facilitated by Pakistan and Qatar is working to prevent a major escalation of hostilities. Iranian negotiators traveled to Doha to participate in indirect discussions aimed at securing an agreement, occurring alongside speculation of potential new attacks following American midterm elections.

Diplomatic engagement gained momentum late last month when US Vice President J.D. Vance addressed a letter to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei, expressing a preference for a diplomatic resolution. This correspondence followed Vance's leadership of the US delegation during April talks in Islamabad. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that if Washington satisfies Iranian demands, the strategic Strait of Hormuz could be reopened within two days, bringing widespread economic relief to Gulf states and the international community.

While the US side has requested guarantees regarding Iran's nuclear program, Tehran has demanded the termination of sanctions, the removal of the US blockade, and other concessions. Both nations must exercise flexibility to ensure the peace process succeeds. The fragile diplomatic progress faces severe threats from planned military actions by Washington and Tel Aviv following the midterms.

US Democratic Senator Chris Murphy criticized the planned military retaliation as insane and capable of triggering a devastating escalation. Simultaneously, the Iranian Supreme Leader has instructed armed forces to retaliate against any aggression without geographical restrictions. Regional governments strongly oppose war due to anticipated devastation, placing pressure on moderate officials within the US administration to prioritize diplomacy and isolate warmongering factions.

stories.title: Asian Stocks Slip and Oil Stabilizes Ahead of US Midterms
stories.summary:
Asian equity markets drifted lower at the start of trading on Tuesday, while oil prices stabilized following a recent tumble. Investors across the region held a cautious stance as voting began for the United States midterm elections, alongside upcoming corporate earnings reports from Apple. Market sentiment was further influenced by ongoing tech sector concerns and regional geopolitical factors.

In regional market movements, MSCI’s broad index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 0.9%, with Korean shares leading losses by falling up to 3.8%. Japanese markets remained closed for a holiday, while Australian shares edged up 0.1%. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index rose 0.3%, whereas Taiwanese shares declined 1.3%. Analysts at ING noted that the trading day served primarily as a prelude to a much larger milestone that would provide market guidance regarding the midterms and US Treasury refunding announcements.

Wall Street stocks also edged lower previously, with the S&P 500 slipping 0.5% due to weaker tech sector confidence, despite positive US manufacturing data for October driven by strong domestic demand. Apple shares fell 2.8% in after-hours trading after forecasting lower gross margins for the holiday quarter because of rising memory-chip costs, alongside lower-than-expected services revenue growth. Meanwhile, the US dollar strengthened against major currencies, and cryptocurrencies remained volatile following a recent major hack involving Binance.

Oil prices steadied after sharp losses on Monday, with Brent crude hovering near $104.72. The previous drop of over 7% occurred as Iranian and Qatari diplomatic talks raised hopes for ending the US-Israeli conflict with Iran and stabilizing crude supplies. However, markets remained sensitive to developments, following reports of a US military strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The upcoming US midterm elections and potential changes in political control of Congress remained central focuses for global investors.

stories.title: Israeli Air Strikes Kill Five Palestinians Across Gaza Strip
stories.summary:
Israeli air strikes resulted in the deaths of at least five Palestinians and left several others wounded in multiple locations across the Gaza Strip on Monday. Medical officials reported that the casualties occurred as Israel intensified military operations amid a stalled, year-old US-brokered ceasefire and escalating regional tensions.

According to medics, two separate air strikes in Khan Yunis caused three deaths and six injuries, while a separate strike in Al-Mussadar resulted in one fatality. Later in the day, another air strike targeted a vehicle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City, killing one person and injuring others. Israel maintains that Hamas has violated the ceasefire by rearming and launching attacks, a claim denied by Hamas, which accuses Israel of undermining peace efforts and blocking agreements over disarmament and troop withdrawals.

The ongoing violence prompted regional reactions, including statements from Jordan’s King Abdullah II. Opening the Jordanian parliament, the king asserted that regional security and stability are impossible without fulfilling the Palestinian people's right to a homeland. He criticized ongoing humanitarian catastrophes in Gaza and relentless attacks in the West Bank and Jerusalem, describing Israel's expansionist ambitions as a primary threat.

In the occupied West Bank, Israeli military forces withdrew from a Hebron neighborhood that had been evacuated of over 3,000 Palestinian residents following a checkpoint attack on October 23 which killed two soldiers. An Israeli military official stated that troops completed searches, detained suspects, seized four weapons, and demolished the homes of the two attackers. The developments coincided with the aftermath of a legislative election in Israel where Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party secured the most votes but failed to achieve a parliamentary majority.

stories.title: Pakistani Government Seeks Allies' Nominations for Electoral Reforms Panel
stories.summary:
The Pakistani government has formally reached out to its key political allies, including the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM), to obtain nominations for the newly proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER). Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry sent separate letters to National Assembly chief whips Ijaz Jakhrani of the PPP and Aminul Haq of the MQM to secure their representatives for the committee.

Mr Chaudhry stated that National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq had already received candidate names from the PPP, though the official roster of committee members will be announced later. According to the agreed representation formula allocating one seat per 16 National Assembly members, the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) will hold nine seats, the PPP five, and the MQM one. Smaller allied parties did not meet the quota threshold, leading the PML-N to allocate individual seats from its own quota to smaller allies such as the Balochistan Awami Party (BAP) and Pakistan Muslim League-Zia (PML-Z).

Addressing the involvement of opposition parties, Mr Chaudhry clarified that the initiative to establish the committee originated with Speaker Ayaz Sadiq rather than the PPP. He noted that while the PPP had engaged with opposition parties, those groups are expected to submit their nominations directly to the National Assembly speaker. Mr Chaudhry expressed confidence that the PML-N-led government would complete its five-year constitutional term despite legislative friction with the PPP.

While acknowledging that the PPP has occasionally complicated legislative processes, the minister emphasized that the party remains committed to the political system. He urged the opposition to participate in the parliamentary committee, viewing it as a constructive step that could encourage broader consultations on critical national issues.

stories.title: Iran Offers to Reopen Strait of Hormuz Amid Intensive Talks
stories.summary:
Iran announced on Monday its readiness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington satisfies strict conditions during ongoing intensive negotiations. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that progress depends on the political rationality of Washington, while Qatari and Pakistani mediators facilitate talks. The proposed framework relies on a condensed version of Iran's September proposal, requiring the US to end military actions, lift port blockades, grant oil sales waivers, unfreeze assets, cancel recent sanctions, reduce regional troop levels, and accept a transit route with Oman.

US President Donald Trump expressed optimism regarding a potential resolution, posting on social media that oil prices were dropping significantly due to growing beliefs that a war with Iran could be avoided. Despite the diplomatic engagement, negotiations in Doha concluded without a definitive breakthrough, and Iranian officials departed while a draft proposal circulated. Iranian sources noted that while a diplomatic deal is desired, a resumption of US military strikes remains a distinct possibility, with Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei warning of an immediate and comprehensive response to any attack.

The diplomatic push occurs alongside the US midterm elections, where fuel prices are a major concern for voters. Meanwhile, international leaders voiced opposition to renewed conflict. Chinese President Xi Jinping, meeting with Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Beijing, warned that the Middle East must not become a battleground for great-power rivalry. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Russian President Vladimir Putin also engaged in discussions with regional counterparts, emphasizing peaceful dialogue, regional energy security, and political solutions over armed confrontation.

stories.title: Oil prices climb following reported US strike on Qeshm Island
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices experienced an upward tick during early Asian trading on Tuesday. This market movement followed media reports that the United States had targeted Iran’s Qeshm Island, an event that heightened anxieties regarding a broader escalation in the ongoing Middle East conflict and potential interruptions to global petroleum shipments.

Brent crude futures increased by 48 cents, or 0.5%, reaching $105.25 a barrel by 0104 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude also went up by 47 cents, or 0.5%, to sit at $96.93 a barrel. These figures followed a previous session on Monday where Brent crude futures had settled lower by $8.66, or 7.63%, at $104.77 a barrel.

According to the Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, the military action on Qeshm Island was characterized by some insiders as defensive measures meant to deter Iranian interference with commercial vessels navigating the Strait of Hormuz. Market analysts noted that the incident injected a fresh risk premium into trading circles just as participants were beginning to factor in diplomatic resolutions.

Diplomatic channels remain active despite the military developments, with Tehran acknowledging ongoing communication with Washington to halt hostilities, following discussions with Qatari intermediaries that produced revised proposals but no final agreement. Meanwhile, the United States and international stakeholders continue to navigate complex geopolitical tensions involving ongoing conflicts in both the Middle East and Eastern Europe.

stories.title: کارل بشبی نے 28 سال بعد 50 ہزار کلومیٹر پیدل سفر مکمل کر لیا
stories.summary:
برطانوی مہم جو کارل بشبی نے 28 برس گھر سے دور رہنے اور تقریباً 50 ہزار کلومیٹر کا پیدل سفر مکمل کرنے کے بعد اپنے آبائی شہر ہل میں والدہ کے گھر واپسی پر جذباتی ملاقات کی۔ سنہ 1998 میں جب وہ 29 برس کے تھے، سابق پیرا ٹروپر نے یہ سفر چلی کے شہر پنٹا آریناس سے شروع کیا تھا۔ اس طویل سفر کے دوران وہ چار براعظموں، ایک منجمد سمندر، صحراؤں، پہاڑوں اور جنگلات سے گزرے۔

ان کے اس طویل سفر میں تاخیر کی وجوہات میں ویزا پابندیاں، 2008 کا مالیاتی بحران جس میں ان کے سپانسرز ختم ہو گئے، کووڈ 19 اور دیگر جغرافیائی سیاسی مسائل شامل تھے۔ سفر کے دوران وہ ارجنٹینا، پیرو، ایکواڈور، کولمبیا، پاناما کے دارین گیپ، وسطی امریکی ممالک، میکسیکو، امریکہ، کینیڈا، آبنائے بیرنگ عبور کر کے روس، منگولیا، چین، ترکمانستان، قازقستان، بحیرہ کیسپین اور ترکی سے ہوتے ہوئے یورپ داخل ہوئے۔

ہل شہر پہنچنے پر لارڈ میئر ماریا کاورڈ اور ایک بڑے ہجوم نے ان کا استقبال کیا۔ اس موقع پر جرمن فلم ساز ورنر ہرزوگ بھی موجود تھے جو ان کی اس مہم پر دستاویزی فلم بنانے کا ارادہ رکھتے ہیں۔ بشبی نے بتایا کہ یہ سفر ان کی شادی ختم ہونے کے بعد شروع ہوا تھا اور وہ اس پورے سفر کے دوران اپنی خریداری کی ٹرالی کو ساتھ دھکیلتے رہے جسے وہ ’دی بیسٹ‘ کہتے ہیں۔

گھر پہنچنے پر ان کی والدہ نے آبدیدہ ہو کر ان کا استقبال کیا۔ بشبی کا کہنا تھا کہ وہ اب اس طویل مہم کو مزید جاری نہیں رکھنا چاہتے تھے اور اس کا اختتام کرنا ناگزیر تھا۔ ان کے اس تاریخی پیدل سفر نے بین الاقوامی سطح پر زبردست توجہ حاصل کی اور یہ دنیا کے طویل ترین پیدل سفروں میں شمار ہوتا ہے۔

stories.title: Americans vote in high-stakes midterm elections testing Donald Trump's power
stories.summary:
Citizens across the United States headed to the polls on Tuesday to cast their ballots in critical midterm elections. The nationwide contest serves as a major referendum on Donald Trump’s second presidential term, potentially shifting the balance of power in Washington by allowing Democrats to seize control of the House of Representatives and challenge for the Senate.

All 435 House seats, 35 out of 100 Senate seats, and governorships across 36 states are currently up for grabs. To wrest legislative control from Republican hands, Democrats require a net gain of just three seats in the House and four seats in the Senate. Pre-election forecasts from Decision Desk HQ projected a Democratic majority in both chambers.

Voter sentiment has been heavily influenced by public frustration over escalating living costs, inflation, tariffs, and fuel prices exacerbated by the Middle East conflict. President Trump’s approval ratings have lingered near the lower thirties, while campaign expenditures have surged past $11 billion in political advertising, supported by substantial financial backing from high-profile figures like Elon Musk.

Ahead of Election Day, more than 57 million Americans participated in early voting, demonstrating high engagement. As polls prepare to close, concerns loom over the certification of results, fueled by repeated claims of voter fraud from Trump and various legal maneuvers by the Justice Department and political campaigns to contest outcomes in specific states.

stories.title: Taliban Expresses Concern Over US Plans to Deport Afghan Migrants
stories.summary:
Afghanistan’s Taliban authorities voiced serious concern regarding reported United States plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants to Pakistan. The reported operation aims to eventually return these individuals to their home country and includes relatives of people who assisted US forces prior to their 2021 withdrawal. Foreign ministry spokesman Abdul Qahar Balkhi issued a statement criticizing the move, noting that the affected individuals have not yet secured legal residency documents in Pakistan.

Advocacy groups warned that removing former allies and their families poses significant risks to their safety. Following their return to power, Taliban authorities declared a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and governments, and they renewed assurances this year that former adversaries can return safely. However, the United Nations has documented various instances of extrajudicial killings, detentions, and other abuses against returning individuals.

The deportation plans stem from broader immigration enforcement efforts by President Donald Trump's administration. Last year, the administration imposed travel bans on multiple nations, including Afghanistan, as part of a sweeping crackdown. Authorities also sought to terminate deportation protections for Afghans who had received special immigrant visas following the 2021 takeover by the Taliban.

stories.title: Britain Extends Residency Wait Period for Foreign Workers to 10 Years
stories.summary:
Britain’s Labour government confirmed plans to extend the waiting period for many foreign workers already in the country before they can apply for permanent settlement. Interior minister Shabana Mahmood announced the adjustments following a lengthy consultation process. The reforms reflect Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s administration attempting to balance public demand for reduced immigration with economic growth objectives.

Under the updated rules, the qualifying timeframe for the Indefinite Leave to Remain status for the majority of workers will increase from five to 10 years. This status allows individuals to live, work, and study in Britain without restrictions while serving as a pathway to citizenship. High earners will qualify after three years, whereas public service personnel like doctors, nurses, and teachers remain eligible after five years. Mahmood stated that the policy will delay settlement for half a million people and save billions in benefits.

Despite the broader tightening, Mahmood softened proposed restrictions specifically concerning social care workers following pushback from ruling party lawmakers. Initial proposals introduced last year would have forced lower-qualified migrants arriving on health and social care visas to wait up to 15 years for settlement eligibility.

stories.title: Emergency Alert Apps in Ukraine and Russia Hacked to Send False Warnings
stories.summary:
Emergency alert mobile applications in both Ukraine and Russia experienced cyberattacks overnight, broadcasting false warnings regarding air raids, chemical threats, and nuclear danger. The security breaches coincided with the expiration of a six-day local ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump in southern Ukraine, marking the longest pause in fighting since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

In Ukraine, the public air raid application began dispatching false notifications shortly before 2100 GMT on Sunday, targeting Kyiv and other regions with warnings of street combat and radiation hazards. One fake message claimed Russia launched a nuclear-capable Oreshnik hypersonic missile. The Ukrainian air force stated on Telegram that the system appeared to be compromised by Russia, noting the alerts were written in Russian instead of the legally required Ukrainian language. Officials quickly issued all-clear messages, and the Ministry for Digital Transformation temporarily suspended the app while traditional sirens and public alerts remained active.

Hours later, Russian state media outlet TASS reported that the Emergencies Ministry's mobile application in Moscow suffered a similar cyberattack. A pro-Ukrainian hacking group named Atesh claimed responsibility on Telegram, sharing screenshots of the breach. The fraudulent Russian notifications utilized profanities, labeled regions as swamps, and falsely warned of nuclear launches while advising citizens to seek shelter in cellars. The Russian ministry downplayed the incident, urged the public to remain calm, and directed citizens to rely exclusively on official websites and verified social media accounts.

stories.title: Seven Migrants Die and Hundreds Rescued off Canary Islands
stories.summary:
At least seven migrants lost their lives off Spain's Canary Islands while over 380 individuals were rescued on Monday, maritime rescue services reported. Coast guard personnel discovered two bodies aboard a migrant boat carrying 132 people approximately 150 kilometers from Lanzarote, noting that five additional passengers had died during the voyage and been discarded into the sea. Earlier on Monday, coast guard vessels rescued another 250 migrants off Lanzarote and El Hierro, following the rescue of 107 migrants near El Hierro on Sunday.

Canary Islands President Fernando Clavijo expressed grief on X, stating that the dangerous Atlantic route from West Africa continues to claim lives. This crossing is widely regarded as one of the most perilous maritime migration paths globally, with thousands utilizing overcrowded vessels to reach Spanish soil despite rough waters and strong currents. Crossings typically rise in autumn due to calmer sea conditions, and a sharp increase in October placed heavy strain on reception facilities across the smaller islands.

Despite the recent surge, total migrant arrivals in the archipelago have dropped 18 percent year-on-year to 11,527 people, according to the Spanish government representative's office in the Canary Islands. In a separate development, Spain returned more than a dozen sub-Saharan African and Asian migrants to Morocco after their asylum applications in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta were rejected. This marks the first deportation of its kind from the enclave since a mass border crossing in July.

The Interior Ministry confirmed the individuals were sent back following Morocco's agreement to receive them, though it withheld exact figures and nationalities. However, local human rights charities and NGOs identified 16 deported individuals hailing from Senegal, Nigeria, Yemen, Cameroon, and Bangladesh. Amnesty International researcher Virginia Alvarez criticized the deportations, arguing that Spain's actions contradict its progressive rhetoric because Morocco fails to adequately respect human rights.

stories.title: Pakistan Private Sector Shifts to Net Borrowing from Banks
stories.summary:
For the first time in the 2026-27 period, Pakistan's private sector has transitioned from retiring debt to becoming a net borrower from banks. State Bank data released on Monday indicated that private-sector net borrowing reached 87 billion rupees between July 1 and October 23 of fiscal year 2027, contrasting with 29 billion rupees in debt retirement during the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. This shift appears driven by government pressure on commercial banks to increase liquidity for the private sector.

Despite this change, the prime minister recently urged the Ministry of Finance to penalize banks that delay loan disbursements intended for farmers, small and medium-sized enterprises, and applicants under the Apna Ghar housing scheme. Analysts note that banks have not supplied sufficient liquidity to accelerate economic growth above levels seen over the past four years. State Bank figures reveal that conventional banks recorded a minimal debt retirement of 320 million rupees, down from 117 billion rupees previously, while Islamic branches of conventional banks extended new loans. Conversely, purely Islamic banks registered a net debt retirement of 63 billion rupees compared to 25 billion rupees last year.

Private businesses remain hesitant to borrow and invest due to several factors, including high borrowing costs, ongoing political uncertainties, domestic terrorism in two provinces, and fears of a regional war. Compounding these hurdles, the State Bank raised the interest rate by 50 basis points to 12 percent last week, further dampening corporate borrowing prospects. Economists and bankers anticipate that further rate hikes may occur in upcoming months because the four-month average inflation rate remains in double digits.

stories.title: Pakistan Launches First Biomass Energy Plant in Sindh Forest
stories.summary:
Pakistan inaugurated its inaugural biomass energy demonstration plant in the Pinnah Reserved Forest located in Sajawal, Sindh. The project aims to support rural livelihoods, decrease greenhouse gas emissions, and alleviate pressure on local forest resources. The initiative is part of the Promotion and Application of Sustainable Biomass Energy Technologies in Pakistan (PASBET) project, managed by the United Nations Development Programme in collaboration with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination.

The facility was jointly opened by UNDP and the Sindh government as the first of four planned demonstration sites designed to exhibit scalable woody biomass energy technologies. PASBET operates as a five-year, $3.5 million initiative aimed at promoting sustainable biomass solutions across Sindh, Punjab, Balochistan, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. UNDP Resident Representative Dr. Samuel Rizk stated that the plant proves rural energy needs can be met without harming forests by converting local residues into clean fuel.

According to UNDP, the Pinnah Reserved Forest site demonstrates how forest and agricultural residues can generate economic opportunities through pellet manufacturing, community tree nurseries, and efficient cook-stoves. These activities foster sustainable forest management while simultaneously enhancing indigenous plant populations. The project's immediate goal is to successfully scale this energy model through coordinated efforts among local communities, government bodies, and market participants.

stories.title: Federal Constitutional Court Reserves Judgment on Super Tax Review Petitions
stories.summary:
The Federal Constitutional Court in Islamabad has reserved its ruling on several review petitions that challenge a previous January 27 judgment upholding the Super Tax. A three-judge bench, led by Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan and including Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi and Justice Syed Arshad Hussain Shah, heard arguments from various senior lawyers representing aggrieved corporate entities and taxpayers.

The challenged tax framework, introduced initially in 2015 by the PML-N government under Sections 4B and 4C of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, applies to affluent individuals, associations of persons, and companies earning over Rs500 million. The levy imposes rates of 4 percent on banking companies and 3 percent on other sectors to fund the rehabilitation of temporarily displaced persons. During the proceedings, numerous corporations—such as Fauji Fertiliser Company, Engro Corporation, Pakistan Refinery, and various banks and industrial concerns—argued against the legality of the tax.

Legal counsel representing the petitioners contended that the retrospective application of Section 4C under the Finance Act 2022 violated multiple constitutional articles by imposing a liability on closed financial years after accounts and dividends had already been finalized. They argued that the levy constituted an unreasonable and arbitrary burden, pointing out that state-owned enterprise losses and electricity theft far outpaced the tax's projected revenue targets. Furthermore, petitioners maintained that denying the carry-forward of losses, depreciation, and amortisation effectively taxes expenses rather than pure income.

The court's upcoming decision is significant because it will determine whether the legislature's retrospective application and execution of the Super Tax via a Finance Act as a Money Bill under Article 73(2)(a) remains legally sound. The final verdict holds immense financial implications for the country's major industrial, financial, and manufacturing sectors that are seeking relief from the contested tax provisions.

stories.title: Balochistan Begins Polio Campaign Amid Cross-Border Transmission Fears
stories.summary:
Balochistan initiated its fifth seven-day anti-polio vaccination drive of the year on Monday, aiming to immunize over 2.2 million children across 31 districts. Health Secretary Mujeebur Rehman announced the campaign launch, highlighting growing anxieties that the polio virus might spread from neighboring Afghanistan, where over 50 cases have been reported this year. Officials noted that cross-border movement poses a significant transmission risk, particularly in border districts such as Chaman and Qila Abdullah.

More than 8,880 mobile vaccination teams have been deployed to reach children under the age of five, with focused efforts concentrated on Afghan border regions and sensitive areas adjacent to Punjab province. During the inauguration in Quetta, attended by Emergency Operations Centre Coordinator Inamul Haq and Quetta District Health Officer Dr. Aimal Mandokhail, Mr. Rehman emphasized that enhanced surveillance and targeted immunizations are vital to stopping potential outbreaks.

Health authorities reported that Balochistan has recorded zero polio cases over the past 24 months, and environmental samples gathered last month tested negative. However, officials warned against complacency, noting that malnourished children and those with existing health issues remain especially vulnerable if the virus returns. The health secretary urged parents, teachers, religious leaders, and the wider community to support the campaign, stressing that total eradication requires unified public and governmental cooperation.

stories.title: Houthi Rebels Advance Near Aden As Saudi Coalition Launches Retaliatory Strikes
stories.summary:
Yemeni Houthi rebels have advanced to within 80 kilometres of Aden, reaching closer to the temporary capital than at any time since 2015, amid fierce fighting with internationally recognized government forces. Military sources reported that clashes are currently underway at a strategic military camp near the entrance to the Tur al-Bahah district, a main access route to Aden. This follows the rebels' recent seizure of the Al-Maqatirah district, which threatens vital transport links between Aden and the besieged city of Taiz.

In response to the shifting ground dynamics, the Saudi-led coalition launched precision air operations targeting vital resources utilized by the Houthi movement. Houthi health ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi reported that coalition strikes hit Ras Issa port and an oil facility in Bajil district, both located in Hodeidah province, injuring a total of seven people. The Houthi official condemned the attacks as flagrant violations of international humanitarian law, while the coalition maintained that the operation specifically targeted enemy military resources.

Simultaneously, the conflict escalated into cross-border drone activity, with Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claiming responsibility for a two-phase drone attack targeting Dammam Airport in eastern Saudi Arabia over a 48-hour period. The group also claimed strikes against a Saudi early-warning radar and a military transport plane in the kingdom's southwest. Meanwhile, coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki stated that forces successfully intercepted and destroyed two drones in the Riyadh area, while Saudi civil defense authorities issued alerts for several southern and western cities before confirming that the immediate threat had passed.

stories.title: Wall Street Journal reports United States conducted strike on Qeshm Island
stories.summary:
The United States recently executed a military strike against Iran's Qeshm Island, according to a report published by the Wall Street Journal. The publication cited unnamed US officials in detailing the operation, which coincided with reports from Iranian state media outlet IRNA regarding multiple explosions on the island located near the Strait of Hormuz.

The military action forms part of a broader pattern of limited, covert strikes undertaken by Washington over recent weeks. According to the reporting, these assaults have been deliberately kept small in scale and out of the public eye to avoid signaling any intent to revive a full-scale military campaign against Iran. The US Central Command did not issue an immediate response to inquiries regarding the incident.

The reported strike arrived on the same day US President Donald Trump expressed skepticism about whether he would pursue further military actions against Tehran. Responding to press inquiries regarding potential post-midterm strikes, President Trump indicated that a diplomatic agreement with Tehran remained a possibility.

The two nations have been engaged in an active conflict since February 28. The ongoing military situation continues to impact regional stability and international markets, even as sporadic diplomatic channels and peace talks are pursued by various intermediaries.

stories.title: Pakistan Literature Festival Concludes Successful Two-Day Event in Houston
stories.summary:
The third Pakistan Literature Festival concluded its two-day run on November 1, taking place across Sugar Land and Stafford within the Houston area of Texas. Organised by the International Academy of Letters USA, led by its president Ghazanfar Hashmi, the gathering convened writers, poets, journalists, intellectuals, and artists hailing from Pakistan, the United States, and Canada.

Event proceedings featured extensive panel discussions on Urdu language and literature, Pakistani culture, journalism, television drama, cinema, youth identity, and contemporary social challenges. Notable figures participated through addresses and panel appearances, including Pakistan's Ambassador to the United States Rizwan Saeed Sheikh via video message, Pakistan's Consul General in Houston Aftab Chaudhry, and Canadian parliamentarian Sameer Zuberi. Sessions explored specific themes such as women's voices in Urdu literature, leadership across cultures, mental health, the evolution of Pakistani cinema, media responsibility, and the nation's future trajectory.

The cultural segment of the festival showcased traditional Sufi music and an international mushaira, which is a classical Urdu poetry gathering presided over by Khawaja Razi Haider and hosted by Mehboob Zafar. Alongside fine arts and book activities, the programme served as a cultural hub for the diaspora.

The primary significance of the festival lies in providing the Pakistani diaspora with a dedicated platform to deliberate on cultural heritage and contemporary issues. A central message emphasised throughout the panels was the critical importance of transmitting a lasting connection to the Urdu language and literature to younger generations while strengthening cultural and intellectual bridges.

stories.title: Karam Ceramics Limited: Historical Performance and Shareholding Structure Analysis
stories.summary:
Karam Ceramics Limited (KCL), incorporated in Pakistan as a public limited company in 1979, specializes in manufacturing and selling wall and floor tiles. As of June 30, 2025, the company has 14.55 million outstanding shares distributed among 306 shareholders. The local general public holds the majority stake at 74.94 percent, while company directors, the CEO, and their children hold 24.81 percent, with the remaining shares distributed across other categories.

The company's financial journey between 2021 and 2026 experienced significant turbulence. Net sales dropped twice during this timeframe, specifically in 2022 and 2025. KCL managed to register gross, operating, and net profits solely in 2021, remaining in the negative financial zone for the rest of the reviewed period. In 2021, net sales surged by 21.53 percent year-on-year to Rs. 1,126.65 million, driven by higher sales volumes, increased selling prices, and a real-estate boom bolstered by government low-cost housing initiatives. Production reached 2.36 million square meters with a capacity utilization of 36 percent, yielding a gross profit of Rs. 35.74 million and a net profit of Rs. 41.63 million.

Conversely, performance deteriorated sharply in subsequent years. In 2022, net sales slumped by 27.39 percent to Rs. 818.08 million due to political and economic headwinds, depressed real-estate activity, and high discount rates. Production fell by 41 percent to 1.392 million square meters, resulting in a thin capacity utilization of 21 percent and a heavy net loss of Rs. 251.76 million. Although net sales rose by 19.44 percent to Rs. 977.13 million in 2023, soaring costs from Pak Rupee depreciation and electricity tariffs pushed the net loss to a staggering Rs. 474.96 million despite capacity utilization dropping to 19 percent.

By 2024, net sales recovered by 38 percent to reach Rs. 1,348.47 million, aided by a 46 percent increase in production and the successful market introduction of a superior-quality brand named "NOVA." Capacity utilization edged up to 27 percent, and workforce numbers were downsized from 369 employees in 2023 to 309 in 2024 to curb payroll expenses. However, a 145 percent surge in gas costs drove the cost of sales higher, culminating in a gross loss of Rs. 418.78 percent for the year.

stories.title: Pakistan Headline Inflation Moderates to 9.6 Percent in October
stories.summary:
Pakistan's headline inflation fell to 9.6 percent in October from 10.3 percent in September, offering some relief regarding the annual rate even as the overall cost of living continues to climb. Consumer prices rose by an additional 1.1 percent during the month, marking the fourth consecutive monthly increase above 1 percent. Over the first four months of fiscal year 2027, inflation averaged 10.1 percent, compared to 4.8 percent during the same period a year earlier, driven persistently by war-driven energy shocks and domestic food supply issues.

Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy items, provided a measure of comfort by easing to roughly 7.6 percent in October from 8.4 percent in September. This suggests that the broader transmission of soaring energy costs remains contained for now, with the four-month average resting at 8.3 percent compared to 7.5 percent a year prior. However, immediate price pressures in October stemmed predominantly from food items. Non-perishable food prices climbed 2.6 percent during the month, standing 9.6 percent higher year-on-year, with rural areas experiencing a sharper monthly increase of 2.9 percent versus 2.3 percent in cities.

Energy remains a primary threat to the economic outlook, with transport prices jumping 28.6 percent and housing and utilities rising 11 percent over the year. Urban motor fuel prices surged by 41.3 percent, electricity charges increased by 22.9 percent, and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices sat roughly 69 percent higher than the previous year, presenting a severe winter risk. Rural households continue to shoulder a heavier headline burden, recording an average inflation rate of 10.6 percent between July and October compared to 9.7 percent in urban centers.

In response to these persistent pressures, the State Bank raised its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 percent to prevent supply shocks from embedding into wider price expectations. Analysts note that while monetary policy can help contain the spread of inflation, structural issues like wheat supply arrangements, LPG deliveries, and power-sector inefficiencies require direct government intervention. If food and energy pressures persist, annual rates could return to double digits through the winter months.

stories.title: Federal Government Announces Rs15 Per Litre Petrol Relief via Refineries
stories.summary:
The federal government has introduced a monthly cross-subsidy arrangement with domestic refineries to provide a relief of Rs15 per litre on petrol, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced during a joint press conference in Islamabad alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar. Under the interim scheme, domestic refineries will absorb an anticipated Rs15 per litre price increase, keeping local petrol prices roughly Rs15 below international market rates at a monthly financial burden of about Rs15 billion. The Ministry of Petroleum scheduled a follow-up meeting with refinery representatives to further refine the operational mechanism.

During the briefing, the ministers highlighted that the government had already distributed Rs27 billion in financial relief targeted at owners of small cars, motorcycles, and rickshaws. The petrol relief initiative was prompted by escalating regional conflicts that have severely disrupted global energy supply chains. Malik pointed out that petrol import premiums had escalated from USD5 per barrel prior to the conflict to USD20 per barrel, while subsequent Pakistan State Oil (PSO) tenders saw premiums spike to between USD25 and USD30 per barrel due to soaring freight, insurance, and logistics expenditures.

With domestic production meeting only about 30 percent of the nation's petrol demand, Pakistan remains heavily reliant on imports for the remaining 70 percent. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar sought to calm public concerns, assuring citizens that the country faces no fuel shortages and national reserves remain entirely sufficient. Additionally, Petroleum Minister Malik dismissed rumors concerning skyrocketing liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, specifically rejecting claims that rates had touched Rs700 per kilogram.

Addressing seasonal energy preparations, Malik confirmed that gas supplies for domestic cooking hours were fully secured for November. Furthermore, he noted that comprehensive supply strategies for the peak winter months spanning December through February were currently being finalized by the government to ensure stable availability.

stories.title: Pakistan October 2026 CPI Inflation Registers 9.6 Percent YoY Increase
stories.summary:
Consumer Price Index (CPI)-based inflation in Pakistan increased by 9.6 percent on a year-on-year (YoY) basis in October 2026, slowing down from 10.3 percent in September but higher than the 6.2 percent recorded in October 2025. According to data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), the CPI increased by 1.1 percent on a month-on-month (MoM) basis in October 2026, compared to a 1.3 percent increase the previous month. Urban CPI inflation grew by 9.5 percent YoY and 0.8 percent MoM, while rural CPI inflation registered a 9.8 percent YoY increase and a 1.5 percent MoM rise.

Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI) inflation rose by 8.7 percent YoY and 1.3 percent MoM in October 2026. Meanwhile, Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation jumped significantly, registering a 13.8 percent YoY increase compared to 13.3 percent in September, alongside a 0.9 percent MoM increase. Core inflation measurements, calculated by excluding non-food and non-energy items, showed urban rates increasing by 7.8 percent YoY and rural rates growing by 7.1 percent YoY, indicating a general deceleration in underlying core price pressures compared to the previous month.
